definition: Despondent means feeling depressed, discouraged, and hopeless.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word despondent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know despondent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The sidewalk portraitist grew despondent as a third straight rainy weekend washed out the art fair.
Disappointed is the sting of one result — it fades by dessert and still expects to try again, which is exactly what despondent has stopped doing.
Deflated goes further than disappointed — the air has gone out of the whole effort for a while; despondent claims the most: hope itself has gone out, and trying feels beside the point.

Dejected is being cast down by one particular blow — a lost match, a botched audition — and it lifts as the blow fades. Despondent runs deeper: discouragement has hardened into hopelessness, and the person has quietly stopped expecting anything better.

Downcast is the sadness you can see — eyes lowered, shoulders slumped, a face gone quiet. It names the look, not the depth. Despondent names the depth: hope itself has drained away, whatever the face is doing.
